title: Public Health Professional Trainings | Overdose Prevention | CDC
content: August 26, 2024 Public Health Professional Trainings About Providing access to relevant training courses for public health professionals on topics related to overdose, opioids, and substance use disorders. Trauma-Informed Care Learning Series This free online course features five modules that aim to equip first responders and post-overdose outreach teams with knowledge and tools to implement a trauma-informed approach to overdose. The course was developed by CDC and the National Association of City and County Health Officials. Teams of first responders – including emergency medical services (EMS), law enforcement officers, and firefighters – respond to people who experience overdose emergencies in the field. They often arrive on the scene first and encounter individuals in crisis. Trauma-informed care is an evidence-based way to: Incorporate understanding of the impact of trauma on a person’s perceptions and behaviors. Promote healing and recovery. Avoid practices that may inadvertently re-traumatize the individual(s) receiving care. The course includes a series of five modules. First responders can earn Continuing Education Units. Module 1: Introduction to Trauma-Informed Care for Post-Overdose Outreach Teams Overview for the series and delves briefly into defining trauma and traumatic stress. Aug. 26, 2024 Module 2: The Effects of Trauma and Toxic Stress The impact of trauma and traumatic stress, and their contribution to substance use disorders. Aug. 26, 2024 Module 3: The Overdose Epidemic Factors that have contributed to the overdose epidemic and its impact on first responders. Aug. 26, 2024 Module 4: Trauma-Informed Care Practical methods for implementing trauma-informed approaches for those who experienced overdoses. Aug. 26, 2024 Module 5: Trauma-Informed Responses Examine how successful overdose response initiatives can positively impact families and communities.
